newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Seagate opens Singapore hard disk plants.
newsitem.headline: Seagate opens Singapore hard disk plants.

text.p: U.S. electronics company Seagate Technology Inc. opened two new computer disk plants here Tuesday, strengthening the city-state's dominance in the production of computer data storage.
Company officials said the two plants, which will employ 900 workers, represented a total investment of about $200 million.

The plants will have a combined annual production capacity of up to 50 million of the 3.5-inch circular aluminium coated hard disks -- equivalent to around half the company's total worldwide disk output.
Seagate is the world's biggest independent manufacturer of hard disk drives and related components, with around a third of the market. It makes 18 percent of the world's disks.
William Watkins, chief operating officer for Seagate's recording media group, said Singapore is an increasingly important centre for the company's operations.
"When we get up to full production, about 50 percent of our media disk production will come from here," Watkins said.

Opening the new plants, Trade and Industry Minister Yeo Cheow Tong said his department aimed to strengthen Singapore's dominance in the electronics industry further over the next few years through the introduction of new companies.
Singapore is already a major centre for computer and computer-related products. Electronics and related products account for almost half its industrial output and about 60 percent of non-oil exports.
"By the year 2000, we hope to produce as much as 30 percent of the world's hard disk media here to support this important industry cluster," Yeo said.
The new plants bring Seagate's total investment in Singapore to more than Singapore $1.2 billion ($851 million).
Watkins said Seagate was taking the current downturn in the worldwide electronics industry in its stride and expected the market to improve again.
